name: What is the difference between a fixed bid and a cost-plus contract?

mainEntity.name: Which contract type is better for a commercial general contracting project with uncertain scope?
mainEntity.text: Which contract type is better for a commercial general contracting project with uncertain scope?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fixed bid works best when the scope is clearly defined and the plans are coordinated, because the contractor commits to a price for the listed work. A cost-plus structure is more flexible because the owner pays actual construction costs plus a fee, which can be helpful when the design is incomplete or hidden conditions are likely. In commercial projects, the wrong contract type can create conflict fast. If the plans are underdeveloped, a fixed bid may carry large contingencies or lots of exclusions. If the scope is very uncertain, cost-plus can be more transparent but requires strong oversight and documentation. Owners should ask how the contractor tracks labor, materials, subcontractor invoices, and markup, and whether there is a guaranteed maximum price or savings-share mechanism. The best option depends on how much certainty exists before construction starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: A fixed bid gives a set price for a defined scope, while cost-plus charges actual costs plus an agreed fee. Fixed bid is better when plans are complete; cost-plus can work better when scope is evolving or hidden conditions are likely. The right choice depends on design certainty and owner risk tolerance.
